stories.title: Myanmar committed acts of genocide against Rohingya minority, world’s top court rules
stories.summary: The Gambia accuses Myanmar of genocide following a 2017 military crackdown that displaced at least 730,000 Rohingya.
stories.detail: Judgment ends seven-year legal battle and is seen as critical test for dealing with most serious of all state crimes Myanmar committed acts of genocide against its Rohingya minority during “clearance operations” nearly a decade ago, the world’s highest court has ruled. The judgment from the international court of justice (ICJ) – which has never previously found a state responsible for genocide – ends a seven-year legal battle and is seen as a critical global test for dealing with the most serious of all state crimes.

details.summary: In case filed at the ICJ in 2019, The Gambia accused Myanmar of breaching the 1948 Genocide Convention.
No state has ever been found guilty by an international court of committing genocide.

stories.title: Trump, Xi and Putin meet as global alliances hang in the balance
stories.summary: President Trump, Xi and Putin have met in Shenzhen for a historic trilateral meeting, with Ukraine, Iran and nuclear disarmament on the agenda.
stories.detail: China's President Xi Jinping on Wednesday pledged to stand up against trade protectionism, while his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin criticized Western sanctions as the two set the stage for a high-stakes trilateral meeting with ‌U.S. President Donald Trump.

stories.title: Israeli tanks cross ‘yellow line’ boundary into Hamas-controlled central Gaza
stories.summary: Hamas condemned the incursion, which the Israeli military said was to dismantle a "terror tunnel", as a "flagrant" ceasefire violation.
stories.detail: First incursion across boundary since ceasefire deal comes as Eisenkot seeks to form government without Netanyahu The Israeli military crossed into Hamas-controlled central Gaza on Wednesday in its first ground operation across the “yellow line” boundary since a fragile ceasefire was agreed last October, forcing dozens of displaced Palestinians to flee their tents. Israeli tanks rolled along the Salah al-Din road , Gaza’s main north-south route, a day after the US-backed Board of Peace, a body overseeing the ceasefire, accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities.

details.summary: Hamas condemned the incursion, which the Israeli military said was to dismantle a "terror tunnel", as a "flagrant" ceasefire violation.

stories.title: Why is Pete Hegseth strengthening US military ties with Venezuela?
stories.summary: Hegseth's new military deal with Venezuela raises questions about US influence, regional security and Maduro's removal.
stories.detail: Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year ago Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro, to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”. Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.

details.summary: Hegseth's new military deal with Venezuela raises questions about US influence, regional security and Maduro's removal.

stories.title: Ontario elementary school teachers become third union to vote for strike mandate
stories.summary: The Elementary Teachers’ Federation of Ontario announced it had overwhelming support for job action.
stories.detail: Ontario English public elementary teachers and education workers have voted 97 per cent in favour of strike action, the union that represents them said Wednesday.
